issues.description: The Stock API in the template uses a method named addItem(StockIngredient) while the problem specification (UML) and the solution use addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). This name/signature mismatch across artifacts can confuse students about which method to call or implement when they follow the UML/specification (e.g., SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery is expected to call addToStockIngredients). Because the template does not provide the method expected by the spec/solution, students may be blocked by compilation errors or be uncertain whether to modify Stock or SealSaloon.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the template's addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (preferred, to match UML and solution) or update the problem statement and solution to accept addItem. Ensure the Stock class exposes the same method name/signature students will use in SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery.

issues.description: The Stock API name for adding a StockIngredient is inconsistent: the problem statement UML and the solution implement addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template repository provides addItem(StockIngredient). Students reading the UML or problem text may look for addToStockIngredients and not find it in the starter code (or conversely expect addItem in the final solution), creating unnecessary mapping confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API name across artifacts. Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add a thin wrapper addToStockIngredients that delegates to addItem) so the template, problem statement UML, and solution use the same identifier.
